clue.text: Confiscates damaged sea-chest

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of the chest are rearranged

explanation.surface: Customs officers impound a battered sea-chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' signals an anagram of SEACHEST. Escheat is an old legal term for property reverting to the Crown or lord.
explanation.definitionFit: To escheat is to seize property for the state or a lord, a legal kind of confiscation.

clue.text: Moral sort of tale about this Roman

indicators.note: about means the jumbled tale goes round the Latin word
sort of hints that the word tale is only roughly itself, rearranged

parts.note: hic is Latin for this, so a Roman would say it

explanation.surface: An upright little story about a Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container; the Latin word for 'this' is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical conduct is principled and right, a synonym of moral.

clue.text: Map change shifts part of France

indicators.note: shifts means the letters of the first two words are moved around

explanation.surface: A change to the map moves a French region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' signals an anagram of MAPCHANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is a historic region in north-eastern France, famous for its wine.

clue.text: Ask to negotiate in French first

indicators.note: first places the French word at the front

parts.note: en is the French word for in
to treat is to negotiate terms

explanation.surface: Asking someone to carry out talks in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; 'first' fixes the order of the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or plead earnestly, a stronger way to request.

clue.text: Swallowing a lot makes voice shake

indicators.note: Swallowing means the word for a voice takes in the letter for a lot

parts.note: a treble is a high singing voice
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a lot

explanation.surface: Gulping down too much makes someone's voice quaver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' is M, the Roman numeral for 1,000, which goes inside TREBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tremble is to quiver or shake involuntarily.

clue.text: Tender is turned back, almost

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed: 'Tender is turned back, almost (6)'. 'Tender' gives the nurse sense of the answer, but no reading of 'is turned back, almost' builds the letters, and no source online gives the parse.

clue.text: Somehow resent accepting little bribe

indicators.note: accepting means the jumbled word takes the small word inside it
Somehow says the letters of resent are arranged in some other way

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: Someone bitterly resents taking a small backhander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' signals the anagram and 'accepting' the container; the Scots word for small goes in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is an inducement or backhander given to win favour, a euphemism for a bribe.

clue.text: Loot given, to chap who camped under a tree

parts.note: swag is stolen goods, loot
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: Stolen goods handed to a fellow who slept under a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls 'Waltzing Matilda', where a swagman camped by a billabong under a coolibah tree.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Australian song 'Waltzing Matilda', the itinerant worker with his bundle camps beneath a coolibah.

clue.text: English copper anticipates trouble right in the country

indicators.note: anticipates means the earlier pieces come before the word for trouble

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: An English policeman expects trouble in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is CU, its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecuador is a South American nation on the equator.

clue.text: Viola disguised, as are these

indicators.note: a disguise alters the appearance, so the letters of the last three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Viola, the cross-dressing heroine of Twelfth Night, is in disguise, as are these others.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Shakespeare's Viola in disguise; here Viola is the plant genus. 'disguised' signals an anagram of ASARETHESE.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild pansy belongs to the genus Viola and has this old folk name.

clue.text: Piece of brass turned to make border

indicators.note: turned means the instrument's name is read backwards

parts.note: a tuba is an instrument in the brass section, so a piece of brass

explanation.surface: A brass object is bent round to form an edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of brass' looks like a lump of metal; it is a brass-band instrument, TUBA, and 'turned' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to lie next to, to share a boundary with, as a verb meaning to adjoin.

clue.text: Edward follows Bobby with lowest sound

indicators.note: follows puts the name of Edward after the other pieces

parts.note: a bobby is British slang for a police officer, as is copper
the bottom is the lowest part
Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Edward comes after Bobby, who has the deepest voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a noise but is the adjective meaning solid and reliable. A BOBBY is a British policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships' hulls sheathed in copper were secure, so the phrase came to mean thoroughly safe and dependable.

clue.text: He'll benefit from opening, in general

indicators.note: in places the word for an opening inside the general's name

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
a gate is an opening in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: Someone stands to profit from a generally open situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' reads like 'generally', but 'in' is the container signal and the general is the Confederate commander of the US Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone named to receive something under a will stands to gain from it when it is read.

clue.text: S-skilful, but not inevitable

parts.note: the stammered S is the letter's name written out
capable means competent or skilful

explanation.surface: A stammerer's skill means nothing is unavoidable.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer gives the name of the letter S as it is written out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Something escapable can be avoided, the opposite of unavoidable.

clue.text: Anne's worried about trap

indicators.note: worried is used in the sense of shaken about, so the name and its s are jumbled

parts.note: the name Anne with its s, taken as letters
re is the Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: Anne is anxious about a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' looks like Anne's mood, but it is the anagram signal, and the S of the possessive is used as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare is to catch in a snare, a synonym of the verb to trap.

clue.text: A low story of degradation

parts.note: a basement is the lowest storey of a building

explanation.surface: A tale of debasement and humiliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story' looks like a tale; it is a storey of a building, the lowest one.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasement is humiliation, being brought low, a kind of degradation.

clue.text: Sporting judge to step outside for an introduction

indicators.note: outside means the word for a step goes round the judge

parts.note: a pace is a single step
ref, short for referee, is the judge in a sporting contest

explanation.surface: A referee steps out to introduce a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'step outside' reads like an invitation to a fight; 'outside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreword at the start of a book serves as its introduction.

clue.text: Blackfoot's one, paradoxically

parts.note: the Blackfoot are a Native American people, and the old dated term for one of them names a different colour and body part

explanation.walkthrough: The paradox is that a Blackfoot is described by colour and body part entirely differently; the term is now considered offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: This dated, now offensive term was used for any Native American, including a member of the Blackfoot nation.

clue.text: Is he coming in to cook the stew ?

indicators.note: coming in means the two words go inside the cooking word

parts.note: to fry is to cook in fat

explanation.surface: A man arrives to make the stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' looks like a dish; it is an old word for a fishpond.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew in the old sense is a pond where fish are kept for eating, a place for breeding fish.

clue.text: Commercial interrupts fight — it's boring

indicators.note: interrupts means the advertisement breaks into the word for a fight

parts.note: a brawl is a rough fight
an ad is a commercial, an advertisement

explanation.surface: An advert break stops the boxing match, which is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like 'dull'; it means making holes, which is what this tool does.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pointed hand tool used to make holes in wood, so it bores.

clue.text: Palm-oil left out of bilberry pie

indicators.note: pie is the printers' word for jumbled type, so the remaining letters are mixed up
out of means the letter for left is taken away

explanation.surface: Palm oil missing from a fruit pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' looks like the dessert but is the anagram signal; 'out of' removes L from BILBERRY to leave BIBERRY, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Palm-oil is old slang for money slipped into a palm, that is, corrupt payments.

clue.text: Loud-speakers in court

parts.note: plays on the saying that deeds speak louder than words, and on lawsuits brought in court

explanation.definitionFit: Legal actions are lawsuits heard in court, and deeds proverbially speak louder than words.

clue.text: Stories about child just a figure of speech

indicators.note: about means the word for stories goes round the child

parts.note: lies are false stories
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: Tales about a child are merely a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal and 'just' a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is understatement by negating the opposite, as in 'not bad', a rhetorical device.

clue.text: Diana's job is a let-down

parts.note: Di is the short form of Diana, so Diana's gives Di's
an appointment is a post or job

explanation.surface: Diana's new post turns out to be disappointing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's Diana is just a name; the split reads her job as her post.
explanation.definitionFit: A disappointing outcome is a let-down, an idiom for failed hopes.

clue.text: An island heaven, so they say

indicators.note: so they say signals that the word for heaven is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: the sky is the heavens above

explanation.surface: Locals call their island a paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: SKYE is an island of the Scottish Inner Hebrides; it is said the same as SKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the largest of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: Kind of affection rejected after Benjamin went out West

indicators.note: after places the reversed word behind the short name

parts.note: Ben is the short form of Benjamin

indicators.note: rejected means the word for affection is turned back to front

parts.note: love is deep affection

indicators.note: out means the letter for West is dropped from went

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for West on a compass

explanation.surface: Benjamin left for the West after his love was spurned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' looks like 'sort of'; 'Kind' alone is the definition. 'rejected' turns LOVE into EVOL, and 'out' removes W from WENT to leave ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A benevolent person is well-meaning and generous, a close synonym.

clue.text: In a frenzy, medium is a catalyst

indicators.note: In signals that the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In a frenzied state, a spiritualist medium brings about change.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are in frENZY MEdium.
explanation.definitionFit: Enzymes are proteins that speed up chemical reactions in the body without being used up.

clue.text: My love's a lady who regrets a bloomer

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O, so love's gives O and s
Cole Porter's song 'Miss Otis Regrets' names a lady who regrets

explanation.surface: A man reports that his sweetheart is sorry about a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a gaffe, but it is a flower. 'Miss Otis Regrets' is a 1934 Cole Porter song.
explanation.definitionFit: Myosotis is the botanical genus of the forget-me-not, a flowering plant.
